corrections.before: if $g$ is $L$-Lipschitz and $g(z)=c\gt0$, then $g\ge0$ on $B_{c/L}(z)$, since $g(y)\ge c-L\,d(y,z)$; a union of such balls is certified.
corrections.after: if $g$ is $L$-Lipschitz with $L\gt0$ and $g(z)=c\gt0$, then $g\ge0$ on $B_{c/L}(z)$, since $g(y)\ge c-L\,d(y,z)$; a union of such balls is certified. If $L=0$, the Lipschitz inequality makes $g$ constant on its domain, so the positive value at $z$ certifies the whole domain; no division by zero is needed.

corrections.before: If $f(x)\ge\ell$ is known and safety means $f\ge h$, every $x'$ with $d(x,x')\le(\ell-h)/L$ is certified without being evaluated.
corrections.after: If $f(x)\ge\ell$ is known, safety means $f\ge h$, and $L\gt0$, every $x'$ with $d(x,x')\le(\ell-h)/L$ is certified without being evaluated. If $L=0$ and $\ell\ge h$, the function is constant on its domain and the whole domain is certified; use this case without dividing by zero.
corrections.reason: The transfer radius requires positive Lipschitz constant; the zero case gives a constant-function global certificate if the known lower value meets the safety threshold.

corrections.after: On $f=\tfrac L2x^2$ with $L\gt0$, the iteration $x_{k+1}=(1-\eta L)x_k$ from a nonzero initial point converges iff $0\lt\eta\lt2/L$
corrections.reason: The zero initial point remains zero for every step size, so the convergence iff requires a nonzero start; dividing by L also requires L>0.

corrections.before: For infima, $|\inf_ta_t-\inf_tb_t|\le\sup_t|a_t-b_t|$ (since $a_t\le b_t+\sup|a-b|$ for every $t$, and symmetrically), so with an $L$-Lipschitz $\bar g$ and non-expansive dynamics the margin $\inf_t\bar g(x_t)$ is $L$-Lipschitz in $x_0$.
corrections.after: For nonempty families of real values $a_t,b_t$ bounded below, with $|a_t-b_t|$ bounded above, $|\inf_ta_t-\inf_tb_t|\le\sup_t|a_t-b_t|$ (compare each family with the other plus the finite uniform difference bound). Thus, with an $L$-Lipschitz $\bar g$ and non-expansive dynamics, the real margin $\inf_t\bar g(x_t)$ is $L$-Lipschitz in $x_0$ provided every trajectory has $\bar g(x_t)$ bounded below; this condition makes each margin finite.
corrections.reason: Real-valued infima require nonempty bounded-below families; the right-hand supremum requires a finite uniform bound. Each trajectory margin must likewise be finite. Without these conditions both infima can be negative infinity and their difference undefined.

corrections.before: A grid of spacing $\Delta$ on $[0,1]^d$ has $(1/\Delta+1)^d$ points and $\ell_2$ covering radius $\tfrac{\sqrt d}2\Delta$
corrections.after: A cubic grid on $[0,1]^d$ with equal spacing $\Delta=1/N$ for a positive integer $N$, including endpoints, has $(N+1)^d=(1/\Delta+1)^d$ points and $\ell_2$ covering radius $\tfrac{\sqrt d}2\Delta$
corrections.reason: An equal-step endpoint grid on the unit cube requires reciprocal integer spacing. The point-count formula can be nonintegral for an arbitrary Delta and is then false as a cardinality. The source now states the actual cubic-grid assumptions used by the exact covering-radius and cardinality proofs.
